distractorExplanations.b: 6.2–6.7 is the commonly cited critical pH for root dentin and cementum; enamel resists until the pH falls to about 5.5.
distractorExplanations.c: pH 7.0 is neutral; enamel is stable there and does not begin to demineralize until the pH falls to about 5.5.
distractorExplanations.d: About 7.4 is blood pH, close to stimulated saliva; enamel is protected at that pH rather than dissolving.
